newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea militant union disappointed at Kim's offer.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea militant union disappointed at Kim's offer.

text.p: South Korea's outlawed umbrella union group on Tuesday said President Kim Young-sam's compromise over a new labour law had not solved any of the union's basic grievances.
"We are very disappointed," the head of the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions, Kwon Young-kil, told a news conference.
"The talks today have not solved any of the basic problems, and are far from what the Korean people demanded," Kwon said.

He also called Kim's offer to suspend arrest warrants for himself and six deputies sheltering at Seoul's Myongdong Cathedral "meaningless unless something is done to resolve suits and complaints against strikers around the country".
Police have arrested five unionists following more than three weeks of stoppages sparked by forced passage of the new law.
Kwon said employers had filed more than 400 legal suits and complaints against confederation members for obstructing business and causing production losses.
